qc.label_under_test: A lexical detector peaking on the psychological word 'nerve', with weaker reliable branches for 'strong' and hit/hurt words

neighbours.label: The noun stem 'nerve(s)' in any language (nerve, Nerven, nerveux/nerveuse, Korean 신경, Arabic عصبية), strongest in emotional idioms (nerve-racking, on my nerves) and weaker in the anatomical sense; not English 'nervous', not stress synonyms without the stem; minor side branch on ' strong' + noun. No hit/hurt branch.
fire: Waiting backstage before my first solo was nerve-racking.
Honestly, the traffic on this road gets on my nerves every morning.
Für diesen Job braucht man gute Nerven und viel Geduld.
Il était nerveux en attendant les résultats.
그는 시험 때문에 신경이 많이 쓰였다.
Penalty shootouts are always nerve-wracking for the goalkeeper.
The surgeon was careful not to damage the facial nerve.
I can't believe he had the nerve to cut in line.
quiet: Waiting backstage before my first solo was terrifying.
Honestly, the traffic on this road annoys me every morning.
Für diesen Job braucht man viel Mut und viel Geduld.
Il était inquiet en attendant les résultats.
Penalty shootouts are always stressful for the goalkeeper.
The surgeon was careful not to damage the facial artery.
I can't believe he had the audacity to cut in line.

predictions: 6-7/8 fire (the anatomical 'facial nerve' and 'had the nerve' are the weak ones), 0 near misses. Context: feeders L5/N5628- (nervous-system medical words) and L7/N1548- (literal veins) are anatomical, yet this + pole prefers the emotional sense of the stem; its - pole carries somatosensory pain. Label option chosen by the stream's Twitch chat vote (default pick, no votes cast); wording tightened after the inverse solver found a ' strong breeze' leak (0.40) and a silent 'pinched nerve' text (0.06).
